authoring.question: e-11507
authoring.value:
Retain the defining inequalities of $R$ exactly. Ordered $z$ bounds require $x\le2x+2$, so $x\ge-2$. A nonempty $y$ fiber requires $(1+x)z\ge0$. For $-2\le x\le-1$, both $1+x$ and every allowed $z$ are nonpositive. For $-1\le x\le0$, keep only $z\ge0$. For $0\le x\le3$, the printed lower bound $z=x$ is already nonnegative. Therefore

$$\begin{aligned}\iiint_R f\,dV={}&\int_{-2}^{-1}\int_x^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx\\&+\int_{-1}^{0}\int_0^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx\\&+\int_0^{3}\int_x^{2x+2}\int_0^{z+xz}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}$$

These three integrals cover the actual region with ordered bounds; boundary overlap has measure zero. For $f=1$, their volumes are $5/24$, $1/2$, and $903/8$, totaling $1363/12$. The source solution used $x\in[-3,3]$ and $z\in[x,2x+2]$ throughout, including reversed or empty fibers; its formal signed integral gives $111$ and does not integrate over $R$.
authoring.rationale: Preserve exact R; remove reversed/empty fibers using three actual base branches.
